statusHistory.note: Amsterdam war-room slate (content/post-plan.md), drafted 2026-08-31 as part of the September 2026 content push. Left in draft, not active, because rules.md's quality-gate-before-publish blocks publishing without a resolved hero image — near-illustrator hasn't been consulted yet, so heroImage is null with strategy pending. The Zeedijk 63 coordinates are also an approximate manual placement (confidence 0.5) and need refining against a real geocoder before this goes live. All facts (opening 1927, Bet van Beeren taking over from her uncle at 25, the tie-cutting ritual, the kissing ban and Queen's Day Orange balls, the 1967 death, Greet van Beeren's 15-year run, the 1982 closure, the 2008 reopening, Diana van Laar's 2007 purchase/ownership, and current hours) were cross-verified across the café's own site, Wikipedia (both the café and Bet van Beeren entries), and the Amsterdam Museum showpiece page, with no contradictions found.

near-illustrator pass: found a genuinely usable, rights-clear source photo on Wikimedia Commons — Tmandje-interior-2022a.jpg, uploaded by user Paul2, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0, showing the actual café interior. Set as hero with strategy 'source' and full attribution. Considered a gallery (there are 4+ same-license Paul2 photos of this venue plus older 1976/2008 shots from other uploaders) but decided against one per the high-bar rule — a single strong interior shot does more work as the hero than a padded gallery would, and none of the other shots clearly show the ceiling of ties that's the actual editorial hook, so a gallery wouldn't add checkable value over the one hero image. No illustration needed: a real 2022 photo of the actual brown-café interior beats a drawn version of the same room.

All six locales complete via near-translator (pt-BR, it, es-ES, es-419, zh-CN, alongside the English source) — full-locale-coverage gate cleared. Hero image and sourcing already resolved. Moved to active as part of the September 2026 content push. Geocode confidence remains 0.5 (manual approximation) — a real address lookup is still owed as follow-up, tracked in BACKLOG.md, but does not block publish per rules.md (only the hero-image and locale gates are hard blockers).
